deep.reconstruction:
The strip is cut on the left, so the first letters of the left-column lines are missing. The surviving parts force a unique reading: the page parametrizes a point of the plane by elliptic (confocal-conic) coordinates with foci at (-1,0) and (+1,0), and then computes the focal distances and focal angles.

Notation (restored by me, consistent with every surviving line):
- c = cos v, σ = sin v (circular functions);
- γ = cosh u, s = sinh u (hyperbolic functions);
- equivalently p + iq = cos(v - iu).

LEFT COLUMN
(1) [c]γ = p, i.e. x = cosh u cos v.
(2) [s]σ = q, i.e. y = sinh u sin v.
(3) [cc + σσ] + ss... read as cc + σσ = 1 = γγ - ss. These are the two Pythagorean identities, cos^2 + sin^2 = 1 and cosh^2 - sinh^2 = 1.
(4) [(1 - cc)](1 - γγ) = -qq. This holds because (1 - c^2)(1 - γ^2) = σ^2(-s^2) = -q^2.
(5) [1 +] pp + qq = cc + γγ. Expand q^2 = (1 - c^2)(γ^2 - 1) and add 1 + c^2γ^2.
(6) [(1] + p)^2 + qq = (γ + c)^2. Add 2p = 2cγ to (5).
   - Hence the distance from P = (p,q) to the focus (-1,0) is γ + c.
   - Likewise (1 - p)^2 + q^2 = (γ - c)^2 (implicit, mine), so the distance to the focus (+1,0) is γ - c.

RIGHT COLUMN
(7) [1 + p = a cos A, q] = a sin A; [1 - p = b cos B], q = b sin B.
   - a and b are the focal radii.
   - A and B are the interior angles of the triangle (focus, focus, P) at the foci (-1,0) and (1,0).
(8) γ + c = a (I), γ - c = b (II). Hence γ = (a+b)/2 and c = (a-b)/2.
   - u = const is the ellipse a + b = 2 cosh u.
   - v = const is the hyperbola a - b = 2 cos v.
   - This is the classical focal characterization of the confocal family.
(9) 1 - pp - qq = ab cos(A+B) = [σσ - ss].
   - ab cos(A+B) = (a cos A)(b cos B) - (a sin A)(b sin B) = (1+p)(1-p) - q^2.
   - By (5), 1 - p^2 - q^2 = 2 - c^2 - γ^2 = σ^2 - s^2.
(10) γγ - cc = ab = ss + [σσ]. This is (I)·(II), together with γ^2 - c^2 = (1 + s^2) - (1 - σ^2).

CONSEQUENCE (mine). The angle at P is π - A - B, so cos(angle at P) = (s^2 - σ^2)/(s^2 + σ^2). Also ab = s^2 + σ^2 = |sin(v - iu)|^2. This is the squared modulus of the derivative of z = cos w, i.e. the metric factor of elliptic coordinates.

Purpose: an auxiliary computation on the map z = cos w (lines go to confocal conics). It is plausibly connected with the neighbouring pages, which concern the 1849 'Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen' (curve figures; a septic with cos φ, i sin φ substitutions on the previous page). The exact link is unsure.
errors: No mathematical errors in the surviving text; every identity checks.

The left-hand portions of all left-column lines and the start of line (7) are lost to the cut. Restorations ([c]γ = p, [s]σ = q, [1 +] pp + qq, [(1] + p)^2, [1 + p = a cos A, q] = a sin A, and the endings σσ - ss and ss + σσ) are mine, but forced by consistency.

results.what: Point parametrized as p = cos v cosh u, q = sin v sinh u (p + iq = cos(v - iu)), with derived identities 1 + p^2 + q^2 = cos^2 v + cosh^2 u and (1 - cos^2 v)(1 - cosh^2 u) = -q^2
results.modern_name: elliptic coordinates / conformal map z = cos w onto confocal conics
results.usually_credited_to: Lamé (elliptic coordinates, 1830s), Jacobi; conformal map folklore of the 19th century

results.what: Focal distances a = cosh u + cos v and b = cosh u - cos v, hence a + b = 2cosh u (ellipse) and a - b = 2cos v (hyperbola)
results.modern_name: focal (bifocal) property of confocal ellipses and hyperbolas

results.what: 1 - p^2 - q^2 = ab cos(A+B) = sin^2 v - sinh^2 u and ab = sinh^2 u + sin^2 v, giving the angle subtended at P by the foci
results.modern_name: product of focal radii / angle between focal radii in elliptic coordinates (metric factor |sin w|^2)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine computation with elliptic coordinates and focal radii of confocal conics, well within standard 19th-century technique and Gauss's known command of conformal maps; only of interest as a working note near the 1849 algebraic-equations material.

checkable.asserts: 1 + p^2 + q^2 = c^2 + γ^2 with p = cos v cosh u, q = sin v sinh u (should give 0)
distance to focus (-1,0) squared equals (γ + c)^2 (should give 0)
distance to focus (1,0) squared equals (γ - c)^2 (should give 0)
ab = γ^2 - c^2 = s^2 + σ^2 (should give 0)
ab cos(A+B) = (1+p)(1-p) - q^2 when 1+p = a cos A, 1-p = b cos B, q = a sin A = b sin B (the expression vanishes identically by expansion)

transcription_corrections: Line 1 left: the lost prefix is c (cos v): 'cγ = p'.
Line 2 left: 'sσ = q' (s = sinh u, σ = sin v).
Line 3 left: 'cc + σσ = 1 = γγ - ss'; the transcription's 'γγ - δσ' is a misreading.
Line 5 left: '1 + pp + qq = cc + γγ'.

Right line 1: the primes on q (and on p in '1 - pp' - qq'') are not meaningful. Read 'q = a sin A ... q = b sin B' (with 1 + p = a cos A, 1 - p = b cos B in the lost part) and '1 - pp - qq = ab cos(A+B) = σσ - ss...'.
Final right line: '= ss + σσ' (cut off).
